:::{#exm-poisson-exponential-family}
#### The Poisson distribution is an exponential family

Let $\Rvar \sim \Pois(\rate)$,
the [Poisson distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-poisson) with rate $\rate > 0$.
Its mass function is a product of a factor free of $\rate$ and a power of $\rate$ times $e^{-\rate}$.
We rewrite it in the form of @eq-exponential-family
by writing $\rate^{\rvar}$ as an exponential of a logarithm:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\pdf\paren{\rvar ; \rate}
&= \frac{\rate^{\rvar} e^{-\rate}}{\rvar!}
&& \text{(Poisson mass function)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\rvar!} \, \expf{\logf{\rate^{\rvar}}} \, e^{-\rate}
&& \text{($a = \exp\paren{\log a}$ for $a > 0$)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\rvar!} \, \expf{\rvar \, \logf{\rate}} \, e^{-\rate}
&& \text{($\log a^b = b \log a$)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\rvar!} \, \expf{\rvar \, \logf{\rate}} \, \expf{-\rate}
&& \text{($e^{-\rate} = \exp\paren{-\rate}$)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\rvar!} \, \expf{\rvar \, \logf{\rate} - \rate}
&& \text{($\exp\paren{a} \exp\paren{b} = \exp\paren{a + b}$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

So the Poisson distributions are an exponential family with
$\basemeasuref{\rvar} = 1 / \rvar!$,
$\statf{\rvar} = \rvar$,
natural parameter $\natparam = \logf{\rate}$,
and $\logpartitionf{\natparam} = \rate = \expf{\natparam}$.

To check the algebra on data,
we use the number of tropical cyclones in northeastern Australia in each of 13 seasons
[@dobson4e, Section 1.6.5],
with the rate set to the sample mean.
We compare the Poisson mass function with the right side of @eq-exponential-family at every observed count.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

##### R

```{r}
#| label: poisson-exponential-family-r
#| code-fold: false
cyclones <- c(6, 5, 4, 6, 6, 3, 12, 7, 4, 2, 6, 7, 4)
rate <- mean(cyclones)

base_measure <- function(x) 1 / factorial(x)
natural_parameter <- log(rate)
log_partition <- function(eta) exp(eta)

exponential_form <- base_measure(cyclones) *
  exp(natural_parameter * cyclones - log_partition(natural_parameter))

data.frame(
  count = cyclones,
  poisson = dpois(cyclones, rate),
  exponential_form = exponential_form
)
max(abs(dpois(cyclones, rate) - exponential_form))
```

##### Python

```{python}
#| label: poisson-exponential-family-py
#| code-fold: false
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.special import factorial
from scipy.stats import poisson

cyclones = np.array([6, 5, 4, 6, 6, 3, 12, 7, 4, 2, 6, 7, 4])
rate = cyclones.mean()

natural_parameter = np.log(rate)
exponential_form = (1 / factorial(cyclones)) * np.exp(
    natural_parameter * cyclones - np.exp(natural_parameter)
)

table = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "count": cyclones,
        "poisson": poisson.pmf(cyclones, rate),
        "exponential_form": exponential_form,
    }
)
print(table)
print(np.max(np.abs(poisson.pmf(cyclones, rate) - exponential_form)))
```

:::

The two columns agree to within rounding error:
the largest difference is `r format(max(abs(dpois(cyclones, rate) - exponential_form)), digits = 2)`.
:::
